ports.name: Porto Novo
ports.description: A bustling harbor city, gateway to inland trade. Grain ships fill the docks.

ports.name: Al-Manar
ports.description: Ancient port famed for its spice markets. Merchants bid fiercely for grain and iron.

ports.name: Silva Bay
ports.description: Timber-rich bay surrounded by dense forests. The shipwrights here are the best in the region.

ports.name: Corsair's Rest
ports.description: A lawless harbor tucked between cliffs. Smugglers, pirates, and those who trade with them.

ports.name: Ironhaven
ports.description: Industrial port city wreathed in forge smoke. Weapons and iron flow out, everything else flows in.

ports.name: Stormwall
ports.description: Fortress port guarding the northern straits. Military outpost with strict inspections.

ports.name: Thornport
ports.description: Whaling town turned trading post. Tea and tobacco are the local currency. Medicines fetch gold.

ports.name: Sun Harbor
ports.description: Golden coast port where cotton bales stack higher than the warehouses.

ports.name: Palm Cove
ports.description: A sheltered cove where rum barrels outnumber the inhabitants. Cheapest provisions on the coast.

ports.name: Iron Point
ports.description: Mining settlement at the river mouth. Iron flows out, everything else flows in at a premium.

ports.name: Pearl Shallows
ports.description: Divers bring up pearls from the warm shallows. A quiet port where fortunes are made by the patient.

ports.name: Jade Port
ports.description: Porcelain workshops line the waterfront. Iron and grain are worth their weight in gold here.

ports.name: Monsoon Reach
ports.description: Seasonal winds funnel the spice trade through this crossroads. The shipyard builds for endurance.

ports.name: Silk Haven
ports.description: Premier silk market of the eastern waters. Rum and iron are scarce luxuries here.

ports.name: Crosswind Isle
ports.description: Free port at the junction of all trade winds. Everything passes through, nothing stays cheap.

ports.name: Dragon's Gate
ports.description: Fortress harbor controlling the eastern straits. Weapons are contraband here, but medicines are gold.

ports.name: Spice Narrows
ports.description: Hidden anchorage in the spice archipelago. The most concentrated spice market in the world.

ports.name: Ember Isle
ports.description: Volcanic island with obsidian beaches. Rich in rare minerals and medicinal plants.

ports.name: Typhoon Anchorage
ports.description: Storm-battered harbor that only the boldest captains visit. Pearls and rare goods reward the brave.

ports.name: Coral Throne
ports.description: Island kingdom built on coral reefs. The king trades pearls for weapons and demands tribute in silk.

routes.lore: The oldest trade route in the Mediterranean. Grain ships have sailed this lane since before memory.
Short and safe — the shipwrights' lifeline. Silva Bay's timber built Porto Novo's fleet.
Every merchant denies using it. Every merchant uses it. The line between trade and smuggling runs through these waters.
Iron from the foundries, soldiers from the fortress. This lane never sleeps.
Thornport's warmth heading to Stormwall's cold. The northern comfort trade.
Mediterranean grain south, Gold Coast cotton north. The route that clothed an empire.
Months of open water. The route that separates traders from merchants. Many set out. Fewer arrive.
From the free port to the kiln masters. Every piece of porcelain in the west passed through here.
Where porcelain meets silk. The two oldest trades in the East, connected by the shortest route.
Named for obvious reasons. The monsoon winds funnel through here like a gauntlet. Timing is survival.
Warm currents and sulfur air. The locals say the sea boils near the islands on bad days.
Timing is everything. Catch the monsoon right and you fly. Catch it wrong and you drown.
Only the desperate or the bold sail this direct. Pirate kings once controlled both ends.
Iron west, porcelain east. The longest profitable route in the world.
Pearl to pearl. The divers of the shallows and the divers of the reef — same craft, different kingdoms.

contracts.description: A port needs grain shipments to feed its population.
contracts.cultural_flavor: The granaries are nearly empty. Without this shipment, the city faces a hungry winter.

contracts.description: A shipyard needs timber to fill construction orders.
Forges and workshops need iron ore delivered.
A port urgently needs medical supplies.
contracts.cultural_flavor: The fever wards are full. Healers work without rest. Every crate of medicine is a life saved.

contracts.description: A military outpost needs arms delivered. Discretion optional.
contracts.cultural_flavor: The fortress needs arms. Don't ask what they're for. The garrison pays well and asks no questions.

contracts.description: Stocks are critically low. Urgent grain delivery needed.
The port's rum stocks are dangerously low. Sailors are restless.
Tea supplies have dried up. The population demands resupply.

contracts.title_pattern: Silk for a private buyer at {destination}
contracts.description: A wealthy collector wants silk delivered quietly.
contracts.cultural_flavor: The governor's daughter is to be married. Only the finest silk will do. Speak of this to no one.

contracts.description: A noble estate requires fine porcelain. Discretion expected.
A spice monopolist needs off-the-books supply. High scrutiny.
contracts.cultural_flavor: The Spice Lords control every legal channel. This shipment goes around them. They will not be pleased.

contracts.title_pattern: Pearls for a royal court at {destination}
contracts.description: A crowned head seeks the finest pearls. The reward is as magnificent as the risk.
contracts.cultural_flavor: These pearls will adorn a crown. The divers who found them will never know. That is the way of kings.

contracts.description: Cotton surplus needs to move. Pays for the backhaul.
A merchant house needs spice moved from origin stockpile.
Textile manufacturers need dyes from the African coast.
Complete a Mediterranean-West Africa trade loop. Deliver goods to prove the route.
Prove the East Indies trade route with a delivery run.
Blaze a trade route to the South Seas. Few have returned with profit.
contracts.cultural_flavor: The South Seas are uncharted profit. Bring back their treasures and your name will be legend.

contracts.description: A premium charter for an established captain. Trust and standing required.
contracts.cultural_flavor: The Exchange Guild only charters captains they trust absolutely. This contract is a mark of honor.

contracts.description: A prestigious North Atlantic trade charter. Only for captains of proven reputation.
The Syndicate needs opium moved from Spice Narrows. Inspection means prison. Success means fortune.
contracts.cultural_flavor: The Monsoon Syndicate controls every pipe of opium east of Crosswind Isle. This shipment goes west. Don't get caught.

contracts.description: Military-grade powder, no questions asked. Deliver to the specified port before the garrison gets suspicious.
contracts.cultural_flavor: Someone needs powder and they need it quiet. The fewer questions you ask, the higher you get paid.

contracts.description: Liberated cargo needs a buyer. Move it to a black market port and make it disappear.
contracts.cultural_flavor: The Brotherhood took a merchant's cargo last week. Now it needs to vanish. That's where you come in.

contracts.description: A pirate faction needs weapons and rum delivered to their territory. Official channels won't touch this.
contracts.cultural_flavor: The faction that controls these waters needs resupply. Help them, and you'll have friends where others have enemies.

armor.name: Leather Vest
armor.description: Stiff cowhide shaped to the torso. Won't stop a bullet, but a blade has to work for it.

armor.name: Padded Coat
armor.description: Layered cotton quilting over a wool core. Surprisingly effective against slashing attacks.

armor.name: Chain Shirt
armor.description: Riveted iron rings over a linen undershirt. The weight is real, but so is the protection.

armor.name: Brigandine
armor.description: Small steel plates riveted between layers of cloth. Eastern craftsmanship, flexible and quiet.

armor.name: Coconut Fiber Armor
armor.description: Woven coconut husk and pandanus leaves, layered thick. Surprisingly tough against blades, and it floats.

armor.name: Steel Cuirass
armor.description: A hammered breastplate from a Northern foundry. You feel every ounce, but blades bounce off.

melee_weapons.name: Cutlass
melee_weapons.description: The sailor's sword. Short, curved, and built for close quarters on a rolling deck.

melee_weapons.name: Rapier
melee_weapons.description: A long, thin thrusting sword. Devastating in trained hands, awkward in untrained ones.

melee_weapons.name: Boarding Axe
melee_weapons.description: Half hatchet, half hook. Made for cutting ropes and skulls in equal measure.

melee_weapons.name: Dagger
melee_weapons.description: A short blade for close work. Fast in the hand, light on the belt.

melee_weapons.name: Kris
melee_weapons.description: A wavy-bladed dagger of spiritual significance. Every kris has a name and a history.

melee_weapons.name: Ida Sword
melee_weapons.description: A broad, leaf-shaped blade from the Yoruba kingdoms. Built for powerful slashing arcs.

melee_weapons.name: Leiomano
melee_weapons.description: A war club edged with shark teeth. The wounds it leaves never heal cleanly.

melee_weapons.name: Halberd
melee_weapons.description: An axe blade on a six-foot shaft. Reach and power, but slow in tight spaces.

ranged_weapons.name: Matchlock Pistol
ranged_weapons.description: A clumsy but devastating single-shot pistol. The slow match glows in the dark.

ranged_weapons.name: Wheellock Pistol
ranged_weapons.description: German engineering. The spring-wound mechanism fires faster and more reliably than matchlock.

ranged_weapons.name: Arquebus Pistol
ranged_weapons.description: A Portuguese trade pistol, common wherever the carracks sailed. Rough but reliable.

ranged_weapons.name: Hand Crossbow
ranged_weapons.description: A compact crossbow that fits in a belt holster. Silent and accurate, but slow to reload.

ranged_weapons.name: Throwing Knife
ranged_weapons.description: A balanced blade weighted for throwing. Cheap, silent, disposable.

ranged_weapons.name: Sling
ranged_weapons.description: A leather sling and smooth stones. Ancient, effective, and completely silent.

ranged_weapons.name: Blowgun
ranged_weapons.description: A slender bamboo tube firing poisoned darts. Almost no damage, but the toxin weakens. Silent as breath.

ranged_weapons.name: Bolas
ranged_weapons.description: Three weighted stones on cord. Wraps around legs, arms, or weapons. More disabling than damaging.

fighting_styles.name: La Destreza
fighting_styles.description: The Spanish science of defense. Every movement calculated, every thrust placed with geometric precision.
fighting_styles.historical_note: Systematized by Jeronimo Sanchez de Carranza in 1569. The first European martial art treated as an academic discipline.

special_action.name: Estocada
special_action.flavor: A geometric thrust — the blade finds the only open line.

fighting_styles.name: Highland Broadsword
fighting_styles.description: The broadsword tradition of the Scottish Highlands and Norse raiders. No finesse, no subtlety — overwhelming force.
fighting_styles.historical_note: Highland sword-and-targe techniques documented across Scotland and Scandinavia. The two-handed claymore was already legendary by the 1500s.

special_action.name: Cleave
special_action.flavor: A devastating overhead arc that shatters guards and bones alike.

fighting_styles.name: Dambe
fighting_styles.description: The fighting art of the Hausa people. The lead fist is the spear, the rear hand is the shield, and the legs finish every fight.
fighting_styles.historical_note: Practiced across West Africa since at least the 15th century. Dambe bouts were a central part of harvest festivals and market days.

special_action.name: Leg Sweep
special_action.flavor: A low spinning sweep — the opponent's legs are taken from under them. They crash to the deck.

fighting_styles.name: Silat
fighting_styles.description: The blade and grappling art of the Malay Archipelago. Low stances, curved blades, trapping hands, and devastating close-range techniques.
fighting_styles.historical_note: Pencak Silat was already ancient when Portuguese traders first documented it in the 1500s. The kris dagger is both weapon and cultural artifact.

special_action.name: Keris Strike
special_action.flavor: The curved kris finds the gap between guard and grip — the opponent's weapon arm goes numb.

fighting_styles.name: Lua
fighting_styles.description: The bone-breaking art of Polynesia. Joint locks, pressure points, and techniques designed not to wound but to permanently disable.
fighting_styles.historical_note: Hawaiian Lua was restricted to the warrior class. Its techniques were so dangerous that training was conducted in secret, at night, under oath.

special_action.name: Joint Lock
special_action.flavor: You seize the opponent's arm and twist. Bone grinds against joint. They can only writhe and dodge.

skills.name: Blacksmithing
skills.description: The art of metalwork — maintaining, repairing, and improving weapons and armor.

levels.name: Apprentice
levels.description: Basic maintenance. Reduce maintenance costs by 25%. Degradation slowed by 20%.

levels.name: Journeyman
levels.description: Field repairs at sea. Reduce maintenance costs by 50%. Degradation slowed by 40%. Can restore worn weapons to standard at sea.

levels.name: Master
levels.description: Master craftsman. Maintenance costs halved. Degradation slowed by 60%. Smith upgrades cost 25% less. Field repairs restore to standard.

trainers.name: Forge Master Erik
trainers.description: The best smith in the North Atlantic. His blades hold an edge for years.
trainers.dialog: "Steel remembers every hammer blow. I'll teach your hands to speak its language."

trainers.name: Old Vasquez
trainers.description: A retired armorer who sharpens blades in the harbor market. Fast and cheap, but not a master.
trainers.dialog: "I can teach you to keep a blade sharp and a pistol clean. That's worth more than fancy swordplay."

trainers.name: The Silva Bay Smithy
trainers.description: A family of shipwrights who also forge the finest blades in the Mediterranean.
trainers.dialog: "We build ships and swords from the same iron. Both need to survive the sea."

trainers.name: Rajan the Tinker
trainers.description: An East Indies metalworker who repairs anything from kris daggers to Portuguese cannons.
trainers.dialog: "Every weapon that passes through this port, I have fixed. Bring me yours."

trainers.name: Kai the Shaper
trainers.description: A young smith who learned from sailors. Basic work, but honest.
trainers.dialog: "I'm no master, but I can keep your steel from rusting in the salt air. That's something."

roles.name: Marine
roles.description: A trained fighter who stands at your side in combat.

roles.name: Navigator
roles.description: Reads the stars and currents. Gets you there faster and safer.

roles.name: Surgeon
roles.description: Keeps crew alive and your wounds clean.

roles.name: Smuggler
roles.description: Knows every hidden compartment and customs loophole.

roles.name: Quartermaster
roles.description: Manages cargo, negotiates prices, and counts every coin.

companions.name: Iron Marta
companions.description: A former garrison soldier who deserted for the sea. Fights like she has nothing to lose.
companions.greeting: A woman in a soldier's coat sits alone at the bar, sharpening a boarding axe.
companions.hire_dialog: "I've been looking for a captain worth fighting for. Pay's secondary. Show me you're not a coward."
companions.loyalty_line: "Best decision I ever made, signing on with you."
companions.warning_line: "Captain... I'm starting to wonder if this ship is heading anywhere worth going."
companions.departure_line: "I didn't leave the garrison to follow another fool. I'm done."

companions.name: Red Tomas
companions.description: A pirate-turned-bodyguard with a face full of scars and a code of honor.
companions.greeting: A scarred man watches you from the corner. His hand never leaves the cutlass at his belt.
companions.hire_dialog: "I protect. You pay. Simple arrangement. Betray me and you'll wish the pirates found you first."
companions.loyalty_line: "You're straight with me, Captain. That's rare on these waters."
companions.warning_line: "This isn't what I signed up for. We need to talk."
companions.departure_line: "The deal's off. Don't look for me."

companions.name: Star Lila
companions.description: A Javanese navigator who reads the stars like others read books. She's never been lost.
companions.greeting: A young woman sits on the dock, sketching star charts on palm bark with quiet concentration.
companions.hire_dialog: "The stars brought me here. Perhaps they brought you too. I'll navigate — you decide where."
companions.loyalty_line: "The stars say we're on the right path. I believe them."
companions.warning_line: "The currents are wrong, Captain. Not the sea — this ship's course."
companions.departure_line: "The stars say it's time to part. I wish you fair winds."

companions.name: Old Henry
companions.description: Fifty years at sea. He's sailed every route twice and remembers every reef.
companions.greeting: An old man mends nets by the harbor, humming a tune you don't recognize. His eyes are sharp.
companions.hire_dialog: "I'm too old to captain my own ship, but I'm not too old to keep yours off the rocks. Deal?"
companions.loyalty_line: "Reminds me of the old days. Good captain, good ship, good sea."
companions.warning_line: "I've seen captains make these mistakes before. It doesn't end well."
companions.departure_line: "I'm retiring. For real this time. Good luck, Captain."

companions.name: Dr. Amara
companions.description: A healer trained in both Western and African medicine. She's saved more lives than most doctors dream of.
companions.greeting: A woman in a clean apron tends to a sailor's wound at the dockside clinic. Efficient, gentle hands.
companions.hire_dialog: "I go where people need healing. Your crew looks like they could use it. I have conditions — no unnecessary cruelty."
companions.loyalty_line: "Your crew trusts you. That's the best medicine there is."
companions.warning_line: "I became a healer to save lives, Captain. Not to watch them wasted."
companions.departure_line: "I cannot stay on a ship that causes more harm than it heals. Goodbye, Captain."

companions.name: Patches
companions.description: A ship's surgeon who earned his nickname from the number of wounds he's stitched. Drinks too much, but his hands are steady.
companions.greeting: A man with rum-stained fingers and a surgeon's kit sits at the bar. He's stitching his own thumb.
companions.hire_dialog: "I can keep your crew alive. Mostly. I charge cheap because I drink the medicine budget. Fair warning."
companions.loyalty_line: "Best gig I've had in years. The rum's flowing and nobody's dying."
companions.warning_line: "I'm a doctor, not a miracle worker. This ship needs better luck — or a better captain."
companions.departure_line: "I'm finding a quieter ship. One where I can drink in peace."

companions.name: Shadow Kai
companions.description: Nobody knows his real name. He makes contraband disappear and reappear wherever it needs to be.
companions.greeting: A man you didn't notice before is suddenly standing beside you. "Looking for someone discreet?"
companions.hire_dialog: "I have skills. You have cargo holds. Let's make each other rich. Just don't ask where things go."
companions.loyalty_line: "Good captain. Doesn't ask stupid questions. My kind of arrangement."
companions.warning_line: "You're drawing too much heat. That's bad for business — and for my neck."
companions.departure_line: "The arrangement is over. You'll never see me again. That's the point."

companions.name: Rosa the Fence
companions.description: A woman who knows the price of everything and the customs schedule of every port.
companions.greeting: A woman with too many rings counts coins at a corner table. She's been watching you since you walked in.
companions.hire_dialog: "Every captain needs someone who knows where the inspectors aren't. That's me. Fifty-fifty on the extras."
companions.loyalty_line: "We're making good silver together. Long may it last."
companions.warning_line: "The margins are getting thin and the heat's getting thick. Watch yourself."
companions.departure_line: "Bad for business, Captain. I'm moving on before your luck runs out on both of us."

companions.name: Coin Mariam
companions.description: A merchant's daughter who can appraise cargo by smell and negotiate prices in seven languages.
companions.greeting: A well-dressed woman inspects cargo manifests at the harbormaster's office. She spots errors in seconds.
companions.hire_dialog: "Your books are a mess. Your cargo holds are inefficient. Your pricing is amateur. Hire me and I'll fix all three."
companions.loyalty_line: "The ledgers are clean, the holds are full, and the silver is flowing. My kind of ship."
companions.warning_line: "The numbers don't lie, Captain. We're heading for a loss if you keep this up."
companions.departure_line: "I don't serve captains who ignore the ledger. Find another quartermaster."

companions.name: Dockhand Pete
companions.description: Knows every dock, every scale, and every harbormaster's weakness on the West African coast.
companions.greeting: A wiry man balances on a cargo crate, juggling oranges. He catches all three without looking.
companions.hire_dialog: "I know cargo. I know ports. I know who's cheating on the scales. Hire me and you'll never overpay for grain again."
companions.loyalty_line: "Good ship, good captain, good cargo. Life's good!"
companions.warning_line: "Captain, I'm starting to feel like ballast. Use me or lose me."
companions.departure_line: "I need a ship that's actually going somewhere. No hard feelings."

merchants.name: Marco
merchants.title: Master Weaponsmith
merchants.description: A stocky Genoese smith with oil-stained hands and a shop full of blades hanging from the ceiling.
merchants.greeting: Ah, a captain with taste! Come, see what Marco has forged this week.

merchants.name: Fatima
merchants.title: Armorer
merchants.description: She runs the finest armor workshop south of the strait. Her chain is tight and her prices tighter.
merchants.greeting: You want protection? Protection costs. But so does a funeral.

merchants.name: Old Silva
merchants.title: Ship Outfitter
merchants.description: A retired shipwright who sells what sailors need. His shop smells of tar and salt.
merchants.greeting: What do you need. I have it or I don't.

merchants.name: Sgt. Gruber
merchants.title: Arsenal Master
merchants.description: A retired dragoon who sells military-grade equipment from a fortress-turned-shop.
merchants.greeting: State your business. I don't sell to tourists.

merchants.name: Widow Kael
merchants.title: Outfitter
merchants.description: She inherited her husband's shop when he didn't come back from the ice. She knows every item by touch.
merchants.greeting: The wind's picking up. Buy what you need before it gets worse.

merchants.name: Hamish
merchants.title: Bladesmith
merchants.description: A Highland smith who forges axes and broadswords in a workshop built into the cliff face.
merchants.greeting: If it's sharp and it swings, I made it. If it's dull, someone else made it.

merchants.name: Adaeze
merchants.title: Arms Dealer
merchants.description: A trader's daughter who turned her father's cloth stall into a weapons bazaar. She haggles like she breathes.
merchants.greeting: Welcome, captain! Everything you see is the best in the harbor. I should know — I tested it myself.

merchants.name: Kofi
merchants.title: Leatherworker
merchants.description: He works crocodile hide into armor that turns blades. His fingers are scarred from the stitching awl.
merchants.greeting: Good leather takes time. I have what's ready.

merchants.name: Yaa
merchants.title: Blade Merchant
merchants.description: She sources knives and slings from inland villages and sells them to sailors at the dock.
merchants.greeting: Pearl Shallows has the best steel on the coast. Don't let anyone tell you otherwise.

merchants.name: Master Chen
merchants.title: Master Smith
merchants.description: Third generation bladesmith. His kris daggers are considered sacred objects in three kingdoms.
merchants.greeting: A captain who values craftsmanship. Please, examine my work.

merchants.name: Devi
merchants.title: Armorer
merchants.description: She imports brigandine plates from the mainland and fits them in her harbor-side workshop.
merchants.greeting: Monsoon season is coming. You'll want something between you and the sea.

merchants.name: Li Wei
merchants.title: Mechanist
merchants.description: A craftsman who builds hand crossbows from bamboo and horn. Quiet weapons for quiet work.
merchants.greeting: Silk Haven values discretion. So do my weapons.

merchants.name: Tane
merchants.title: Warrior Outfitter
merchants.description: A former reef warrior who now outfits captains with the weapons of his people.
merchants.greeting: The reef teaches you to fight or it teaches you to drown. Which are you?

merchants.name: Malia
merchants.title: Outfitter
merchants.description: She runs the only proper shop between the reefs. If she doesn't have it, you don't need it.
merchants.greeting: Typhoon Anchorage! Where the brave come to buy and the foolish come to sell.

style_masters.name: Maestro Luciano
style_masters.description: A retired fencing master who teaches the Spanish school from a warehouse overlooking the harbor.
style_masters.dialog: "The sword is a compass. Your body is the circle. Step correctly and no blade can touch you."

style_masters.name: Señora Vega
style_masters.description: A Castilian expatriate who runs the only fencing school east of Gibraltar.
style_masters.dialog: "You fight like a dockhand. I will teach you to fight like a mathematician."

style_masters.name: Red Hamish
style_masters.description: A massive Scotsman with arms like anchor chains. He teaches broadsword in the foundry yard, sparking steel against iron.
style_masters.dialog: "Ye dinnae need fancy footwork when ye can split a man's shield in two. Hit harder. Again."

style_masters.name: Jarl Solveig
style_masters.description: A Norse shieldmaiden who settled in Thornport after twenty years of raiding. She teaches the old ways.
style_masters.dialog: "The broadsword is not a weapon. It is a statement. When you swing, mean it."

style_masters.name: Kolo the Fist
style_masters.description: A retired champion whose wrapped fists have broken more guards than any siege engine. He teaches on the beach at dawn.
style_masters.dialog: "The spear fist strikes. The shield hand protects. The leg decides. Simple. Now do it a thousand times."

style_masters.name: Nneka Ironfist
style_masters.description: A woman who earned her name in the fighting circles of the Gold Coast. She teaches with bruises, not words.
style_masters.dialog: "You think fighting is about your arms? Your legs carry the fight. Everything begins from the ground."

style_masters.name: Pak Reza
style_masters.description: An elderly silat master who moves like smoke. His school is hidden behind a porcelain shop.
style_masters.dialog: "The kris is not a sword. It does not cut — it finds. Every body has openings. I will teach you to see them."

style_masters.name: Dewi Ayu
style_masters.description: A trader's daughter who learned silat from her grandmother. She teaches in the monsoon rain because 'the deck is always wet.'
style_masters.dialog: "Western fencing stands tall and proud. Silat crouches low and survives. Which do you think lasts longer at sea?"

style_masters.name: Kahoku the Elder
style_masters.description: An ancient warrior-priest whose hands have set more bones than any doctor — because he broke them first.
style_masters.dialog: "Lua was never meant for sport. Every hold is designed to end a fight permanently. Are you certain you want this knowledge?"

style_masters.name: Leilani Bonecatcher
style_masters.description: A young woman with an old name. She learned Lua from her grandfather and teaches it to those the sea has tested.
style_masters.dialog: "The bones tell you everything. How strong they are, where they bend, where they break. Listen to the bones."

milestones.name: First Warehouse
milestones.description: Leased your first warehouse — cargo can now be staged for timing plays.

milestones.name: First Broker Office
milestones.description: Opened your first broker office — intelligence shapes the contract board.

milestones.name: Regional Standing
milestones.description: Reached meaningful standing in one region through consistent commerce.

milestones.name: Strong Regional Presence
milestones.description: Achieved strong standing in one region — a known and respected operator.

milestones.name: Two-Region Presence
milestones.description: Established operations in two different regions.

milestones.name: Credible Operator
milestones.description: The market recognizes you as credible — new opportunities open.

milestones.name: Reliable Operator
milestones.description: Reliable commercial trust — premium contracts and better credit terms.

milestones.name: First Regional Charter
milestones.description: Acquired your first regional trade charter — formal commercial standing.

milestones.name: High Reputation Charter
milestones.description: Earned the highest commercial charter — recognized across all regions.

milestones.name: Proven Contract Record
milestones.description: Completed 5+ contracts — a track record of reliable delivery.

milestones.name: Clean Growth
milestones.description: Reached reliable trust while keeping heat low — growth without suspicion.

milestones.name: First Discreet Delivery
milestones.description: Completed your first discreet luxury delivery — the shadow lane is open.

milestones.name: Operating Under Scrutiny
milestones.description: Sustained high heat while remaining profitable — the authorities watch, but you persist.

milestones.name: Shadow Profitability
milestones.description: Strong net profit despite elevated customs scrutiny.
